title: SLO-driven admission gate and attention-adaptive routing
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Goal: Reduce 99th/99.9th token latency across mixed workloads by combining an SLO-driven admission gate, attention-pattern aware routing to kernel variants, and a lightweight decode pacing layer. Background: existing admission batchers admit based on queue age and batch fullness. That approach yields good median latency but suffers tail spikes when attention-density or KV-cache locality changes cause kernel slowdowns. This ticket explores a combined control path: (1) an SLO admission gate that enforces per-tenant P99 budget windows, (2) an attention-pattern classifier that routes prefill/decode jobs to kernels optimized for sparse/dense attention (and optionally quantized variants), and (3) a decode pacing shim that staggers large-token decodes to avoid downstream kernel head-of-line blocking. Success criteria: 10-20% reduction in P99 token latency on production-like traces, no >5% regression in median latency, and stable throughput within 95% of current baseline for large decode workloads.
